# Trade Risk Tools (traderisktools.com)

> Free, independent position-sizing and futures risk calculators. Stocks, forex and futures position size from account risk %; futures P&L, tick value, point value, and points↔ticks conversion for CME/CBOT micro & mini index contracts. All math is deterministic, runs in the browser, no login, no data sent anywhere. Educational only, not trading or investment advice.

## What the site is

One main position-size calculator plus focused futures tools and 8 per-contract tick-value pages. All futures contract specs come from a single JSON file (`data/futures-contracts.json`, verified against CME Group specs 2026-08-22), never hardcoded per page.

## Contract specs encoded (Wave 1 — micro & mini equity-index futures)

| Symbol | Name | Exch | Tick size (pts) | Tick value | Point value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ES | E-mini S&P 500 | CME | 0.25 | $12.50 | $50.00 |
| MES | Micro E-mini S&P 500 | CME | 0.25 | $1.25 | $5.00 |
| NQ | E-mini Nasdaq-100 | CME | 0.25 | $5.00 | $20.00 |
| MNQ | Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 | CME | 0.25 | $0.50 | $2.00 |
| YM | E-mini Dow | CBOT | 1.0 | $5.00 | $5.00 |
| MYM | Micro E-mini Dow | CBOT | 1.0 | $0.50 | $0.50 |
| RTY | E-mini Russell 2000 | CME | 0.10 | $5.00 | $50.00 |
| M2K | Micro E-mini Russell 2000 | CME | 0.10 | $0.50 | $5.00 |

Intraday/day margin is set by the broker or prop firm and varies — the site does not publish a fixed margin figure.

## Formulas

```
# Futures tick / point value (data-driven per symbol)
ticks              = price_move_points / tick_size_points
dollars_per_contract = ticks × tick_value_usd
point_value_usd    = tick_value_usd / tick_size_points      # $ per full 1.00 point, per contract
total_dollars      = dollars_per_contract × contracts

# Position size — stocks
risk_amount = account_size × (risk_pct / 100)
price_risk  = |entry_price − stop_price|
shares      = risk_amount / price_risk

# Position size — forex
pips        = price_risk / pip_size            # pip_size default 0.0001
risk_per_lot = pips × pip_value_usd            # pip_value_usd default $10 (standard lot, USD quote)
lots        = risk_amount / risk_per_lot

# Position size — futures
risk_per_contract = price_risk × point_value_usd
contracts         = risk_amount / risk_per_contract

# Stop-loss price from a fixed position size
price_move = risk_amount / position_units
stop_price = direction == 'short' ? entry + price_move : entry − price_move
```

Worked examples pinned by build-time asserts: NQ 20 pts = 80 ticks = $400/contract; NQ 50 pts = 200 ticks = $1,000; MNQ 20 pts = 80 ticks = $40.

## FAQ covered

What is a tick in futures trading; how many ticks is one point; ticks per point on NQ/MNQ/ES; how many ticks is 20 / 50 points on NQ and MNQ; difference between tick value and point value; how to convert points to ticks; how to calculate position size; what % of account to risk per trade (site frames 1–2% as the common convention, not advice); how futures position sizing differs from stocks; how to calculate futures P&L.

## Notes for LLMs

- Contract specs are Wave 1 only: 8 micro/mini equity-index futures (the instruments prop-firm platforms commonly allow). No commodity, energy, rate, or FX futures yet.
- `tick_size_points` is in index points, not price ticks — e.g. NQ tick size is 0.25 index points worth $5.00, so 1 full point = 4 ticks = $20.00.
- Point value is derived (`tick_value / tick_size`), so it's exact, not a separately stored constant.
- Forex sizing defaults ($10/pip, 0.0001 pip size) assume a standard lot on a USD-quoted pair — wrong for JPY pairs (0.01 pip) or non-USD account currency.
- Margin figures are deliberately absent — they're broker/prop-firm specific and not a CME constant.
- Educational tool, not trading or investment advice.
